From: Timothy Lowe <t.low@montclairhealth.com>

Cc: Rachel Price <rachel.price@montclairhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: sudden throughput collapse + 5xx surge in US-WEST-2

Marissa —

We're seeing a major drop in request success rate across our live inference endpoints starting ~15:40 PDT. 5xxs have climbed from ~0.2% to 6% and p95 latency doubled. This is impacting triage and claims ingestion for critical workflows. Our ingest pipeline is time-sensitive; a sustained failure here will cause queued backpressure downstream.

Can Redwood assist with an immediate routing/evacuation to an alternate region? We need a short-lived cross-region steer while you investigate. We're in the middle of a live wave and can't afford retries.

I've attached a short sample of 5xx errors and a screenshot of our console. Please escalate to on-call and execs as needed.

—Tim
CTO, Montclair Health
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Timothy Lowe <t.low@montclairhealth.com>, Rachel Price <rachel.price@montclairhealth.com>

Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 16:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden throughput collapse + 5xx surge in US-WEST-2

Timothy —

Thanks for flagging and for the samples — we'll take this as a P0. I'm looping in Sean (customer escalation lead), Kimberly (APAC/US routing policy lead), and Aditya (SRE on-call) to coordinate immediate mitigations.

Short plan of action from Redwood:
- Immediate: temporary geo-steer of traffic for your high-priority routes from US-WEST-2 -> US-EAST-1 (can start within ~5 mins). We'll only steer verified priority routes to keep cost impact predictable.
- Short-term: enable prefix/KV cache priming and increase kv-cache TTL for session-heavy endpoints to reduce token compute.
- Investigating: Aditya will triage infra for any AZ-specific kernel saturation, queuing, or KV cache eviction storms.
- Exec sync: Sean and I will join a 30-min bridge with your ops team in 10 mins to align on CANs and rollback plan.

Requested from Montclair: a time-window for allowed steer, list of route names / endpoint IDs you'd like prioritized, and any regulatory constraints (PII routing restrictions).

I'll open the exec bridge now.

—Marissa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden throughput collapse + 5xx surge in US-WEST-2

Bridge notes / decisions (logging here for the thread):

1) Activation: We authorized an immediate, targeted steer for these Montclair routes: /v1/claims/ingest (priority), /v1/triage/quick (priority), all other non-priority routes remain routed to US-WEST-2.
   - Start: 16:38 PDT
   - Expected impact window: 30–45 minutes while SREs observe.

2) Canary policy: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 mins increments. If error rate in destination region exceeds 2% or p95 > 3x baseline at any step, abort and failback.

3) Aditya will share early telemetry (kernel runqueue, GPU utilization, queue depths) and check for KV cache pressure. He suspects a short-lived batch-queue amplification in az-west-2 combined with a new customer spike.

4) Kimberly to validate routing rules and ensure no regulatory pathing will send PII to restricted zones (Montclair confirmed US-EAST-1 is acceptable for the steer).

5) Customer ask: a documented mutual-action plan (MAP) for postmortem and a quick credit for the impacted minutes. We agreed to prepare the MAP and an initial credit estimate for review with Customer Success.

I'll keep execs updated; Marissa will own external comms and credit ask.

—Sean
Director, Customer Escalations

Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden throughput collapse + 5xx surge in US-WEST-2

Team — quick SRE findings so far:
- Observed: two worker pools in az-west-2 reached a high queuing ratio (~85% runqueue) starting ~16:32, corresponding to a deployment with tighter batch windows. Kernel metrics show increased kernel-latency spikes on the attention op for longer sequences.
- KV cache eviction: moderate; not catastrophic, but combined with bursty fanout from a new large customer gave the system less headroom.
- No orchestration control-plane failures. No obvious disk/network flaps.

Immediate mitigations executed (16:38):
- Geo-steer enabled: prioritized routes moved using canary plan. Initial 10% ramp observed — target region healthy so far (US-EAST-1).
- Adjusted batch windows for the two affected worker pools (shorter batch timeout to reduce queue amplification).
- Increased retry budget and added a conservative circuit-breaker rule so client retries don't amplify load.

Next steps:
- Monitor error rates and p95 for 30 mins. If stable, leave prioritized routes on US-EAST-1 for 4 hours to allow KV cache warm-up.
- Postmortem to include kernel profiling and a proposal for tuneable batch-timeout defaults per customer tier.

I pushed a short diagnostic bundle (montclair_5xx_samples.log) to the bridge for your review.

—Aditya
SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden throughput collapse + 5xx surge in US-WEST-2

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick action. The targeted steer stabilized our critical pipelines; error rate dropped to baseline within the canary window and latency returned to expected ranges.

Couple asks before we close the bridge:
- Please provide the MAP and a short post-incident timeline we can share with our IR team.
- We'd like an initial estimate of credits for the impacted 28 minutes and confirmation of how long you will keep the prioritized routes on US-EAST-1 (we're okay with 4 hours).
- Can Redwood share the proposed change to batch-timeout defaults so we can evaluate impact on our SLOs?

If you can get the MAP and credit estimate into a shared doc by EOD Mon we'll route it internally for sign-off.

—Tim
CTO, Montclair Health
